walkthroughs.body_html:
Resources & Their Management — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Resources & Their Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Resources & Their Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued food can't keep up with population (1798)?
options: Darwin
Malthus
Marx
Smith

mcqs.q: Shift from high to low birth/death rates is called?
options: Demographic transition
Carrying capacity
Population pyramid
Mortality crisis

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Bacteria produce them.
Environmental protection at all costs.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: Bacteria produce them.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
Stopping all development immediately.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
Bacteria produce them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Demographic transition”?
options: Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.
Area of productive land needed to sustain a person's consumption and absorb their waste.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Carrying capacity”?
options: Area of productive land needed to sustain a person's consumption and absorb their waste.
Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resource depletion”?
options: Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Faster use of non-renewables (minerals, fossil fuels) than they form or can be substituted.
Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Malthusian theory”?
options: Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Population pyramid”?
options: Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.
Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.
Faster use of non-renewables (minerals, fossil fuels) than they form or can be substituted.

options: Area of productive land needed to sustain a person's consumption and absorb their waste.
